pure-announcement.rationale: This is a first-person account of security architecture and practices across an AI-native SDLC, not a launch or release note for any product.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concept siem-agentic-visibility-gap touches only the SIEM-routing point; the closed-loop guideline encoding, agent containment, and review-governance material is new relative to all six neighbours.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The practices are described mechanistically and the headline numbers (16-to-54% substantive review rate, Intercom's 19% auto-approvals, 500 OSS vulnerabilities) are linked to primary sources.

durability.rationale: The stated enduring principles - close the loop from bug class to generation-time instructions, bound agents by access rather than instructions, review with multiple narrow agents - are architecture-level trade-offs that outlive the specific tooling named.

actionability.rationale: A security team could directly adopt the concrete controls described: egress-allowlisted VMs, risk-tiered automation, shadow mode for new reviewers, sampled approvals, and routing every agent action to the SIEM.

atomicity.rationale: The note bundles at least four standalone concepts - closed-loop secure-codegen instructions, least-agency identity boundaries for agents, multi-agent narrow-scope review, and loop-governance controls - each of which stands alone without the SDLC-stage framing.
